I will still put most of my land into `wheat-maize` this year, same as before, because that is the safest way for me to hold yield and cash. I have 16.1 mu and only 2 people at home, so I cannot spread myself too thin on crops that need too much hand work. I will keep `10 mu` in winter wheat, then after harvest I will follow that same `10 mu` with summer maize. The rest I will split into smaller pieces: `2 mu` cotton, `1.5 mu` millet, `1 mu` mung bean, and `1.6 mu` peanut. That way I still have the crops I know, but my main income stays on the land that gives steady grain.

For fertilizer, I will do it the practical way I have used for years, with a little adjustment where I think the crop pulls harder. Wheat and maize will get the heaviest feeding because if those two fail, the whole year feels bad. I would rather spend a bit more fertilizer money than watch yield drop. Cotton and peanut I will also feed properly, especially phosphorus and potassium, because I have seen weak bottom fertilizer give empty bolls and poor pod set. Millet and mung bean I will keep lighter, especially nitrogen, because pushing them too hard is wasted money and can make them grow too much vine or straw. Since I have well irrigation, I will not let wheat miss water at jointing and grain filling, and I will give maize water around big flare and grain set if the rain is short. I will keep tillage simple, mostly rotary or plough where the soil needs loosening, so the work fits my age and my family labor.
